title: Claims summary per customer (NULL, type and aggregation semantics)
businessPurpose: Claims management wants one line per insured customer with a contact label, how many claims, the amount claimed, the average amount paid (unpaid counts as 0) and the share still open.

invariants.name: one row per customer that has a policy

candidates.why: COALESCE in the label and the average, a numeric cast for the ratio.
|| with a NULL email returns NULL in PostgreSQL but an empty piece in Oracle. Executable, plausible, wrong for customer 2.
bigint / bigint truncates: the open ratio is 0 wherever it should be a fraction.
AVG ignores NULL paid amounts, so averages are higher than Oracle's AVG(NVL(x,0)).
COUNT(*) counts the null-extended row for a customer without claims.
The right rows in the wrong order: ORDER BY customer_id DESC where the legacy query sorts ascending. Same multiset of rows, so only the row-order check sees it.
The NULL-email label is special-cased for customer 2. Right on the primary data, wrong for any other customer without an email.
